episodes.215810: A backdoor front moved through much of eastern New Mexico during the morning hours of August 25th as the center of a very strong upper high moved over south central New Mexico. Higher moisture and upslope surface flow behind the backdoor front resulted in thunderstorm development across the east slopes of the central mountain chain midday with thunderstorms moving east and southeast across the eastern plains during the afternoon and early evening hours. Thunderstorms produced severe wind gusts at Clayton Municipal Airport and at a ZiaMet station east of Fort Sumner before exiting into West Texas around sunset. Upslope surface flow continued across eastern New Mexico on August 26th resulting in strong to severe thunderstorm development across this part of the state. One thunderstorm brought some severe hail to Dilia in far northwest Guadalupe County. Storms coalesced into a line across east central and southeast New Mexico during the evening hours before exiting into West Texas around midnight.
episodes.216479: Isolated to scattered strong to severe storms moved across the CWA to the north and south of the North Platte River Valley. Several storms produced large hail with one storm producing damaging winds.
episodes.216851: Large hail fell across north central South Dakota, with a public report of hail slightly larger than baseballs 4 miles west of Mound City, while thunderstorm winds topped out at 71 mph on the South Dakota State University mesonet station 9 miles north northwest of Murdo.
episodes.217013: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.
episodes.217544: NDBC buoy gusted to 35 knots from a thunderstorm.
episodes.217560: Heavy rain over southern Utah eventually would send a flash flood down the Paria River to the Colorado River confluence at Lee's Ferry.
episodes.217604: On the late afternoon and evening of August 25, 2026, isolated severe thunderstorms tracked across northeastern Minnesota as increasingly moist airmass interacted with an approaching front. Some of the storms produced 60 mph wind gusts and large hail leading to downed trees and power lines across St. Louis County communities���including areas near Rice Lake, Kelsey, and Morgan Park���alongside hail up to 1.25 inches in diameter reaching into neighboring Carlton and Pine counties.
episodes.217642: Remnant convection across western Oklahoma gradually intensified as it approached a quasi-stationary boundary during the afternoon and early evening of the 25th. Sufficient wind shear and instability produced transient supercells and organized thunderstorm clusters, leading to reports of large hail, severe wind gusts and wind damage.
episodes.217643: Remnant convection across western Oklahoma gradually intensified as it approached a quasi-stationary boundary during the afternoon and early evening of the 25th. Sufficient wind shear and instability produced transient supercells and organized thunderstorm clusters, leading to reports of large hail, severe wind gusts and wind damage.
episodes.217733: A broad sub-tropical ridge axis was centered to the west of the area over Texas and the southern Plains resulting in a deep layer northerly flow regime in the mid and upper levels of the atmosphere. Additionally, a stationary front extended east-southeastward from central Louisiana toward Lower Alabama across southwest Mississippi. A line of of strong to severe thunderstorms developed along the stationary frontal boundary over the Northshore region of southeast Louisiana and then swept southwestward through southeast Louisiana during the afternoon hours. The severe storms within the line produced damaging wind gusts and hail.
episodes.217734: A broad sub-tropical ridge axis was centered to the west of the area over Texas and the southern Plains resulting in a deep layer northerly flow regime in the mid and upper levels of the atmosphere. Additionally, a stationary front extended east-southeastward from central Louisiana toward Lower Alabama across southwest Mississippi. A line of of strong to severe thunderstorms developed along the stationary frontal boundary over the Northshore region of southeast Louisiana and then swept southwestward across Lake Pontchartrain during the afternoon hours. The severe storms within the line produced severe marine thunderstorm wind gusts in Lake Pontchartrain.
episodes.217869: A weather system moved through on August 25th and brought favorable conditions for severe thunderstorms across the Texas Panhandle. A line of thunderstorms developed in the afternoon and became widespread through the evening as it moved from northwest to southeast. Damaging winds were the primary hazard, but these storms also produced some hail and caused flash flooding in some areas.
episodes.217870: A weather system moved through on August 25th and brought favorable conditions for severe thunderstorms across the western Oklahoma Panhandle. A line of thunderstorms developed in the afternoon and became widespread through the evening, but Oklahoma only suffered from northern portions of the line. Damaging winds were the primary hazard.
episodes.217940: A frontal boundary dropped southward into southern GA on the 24th before stalling into the 25th. This, combined with some weak upper level energy and influences from southwest flow and the Atlantic sea breeze, resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms and isolated strong to severe cells across northeast FL. Impacts were mainly due to heavy rainfall from slow moving storms, though isolated thunderstorm wind damage also occurred.
episodes.217941: Several supercells produced very large hail over parts of the Devils Lake Basin during the evening hours. The largest measured hail size was 3.25 inches in Nelson County ND.
episodes.217943: A severe thunderstorm produced severe winds in southwest Marshall County, MN during the evening hours.
episodes.218189: A surface trough pushed east through the state during the afternoon and evening, with the center of the low traversing the southern Canadian Prairies. A cluster of supercells developed and produced large hail in the northern James River Valley, before consolidating into a line as they moved south and produced damaging thunderstorm wind gusts in McIntosh County. The strongest measured wind gust was 77 mph in Wishek, and the largest hail was 1.5 inches in diameter near Woodworth in Stutsman County.
episodes.218211: A warm and increasingly moist airmass along with a stationary front nearby supported thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds.
episodes.218212: A warm and increasingly moist airmass along with a stationary front nearby supported thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds.
episodes.218222: On August 21st and 22nd, a mid level shortwave moved through southeast Georgia and interacted with sea breeze and outflow boundaries to produce scattered to numerous showers and storms. Cooler than normal temperatures aloft from -7C to -8C at 500 mb increased mid level lapse rates which supported a couple of strong to severe thunderstorms. Another frontal boundary dropped southward into northern GA on the 23rd, into southern GA on the 24th before stalling into the 25th. This, combined with some weak upper level energy and influences from southwest flow and the Atlantic sea breeze, resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms and isolated strong to severe cells.
episodes.218293: An isolated elevated thunderstorm developed near a cold front which stalled across east central South Dakota during the early morning hours.  Supported by a weak low-level jet, this storm intensified briefly to produce marginally large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.218478: The subtropical ridge established itself once again with weak troughing off the Pacific Northwestern U.S. coastline. With robust moisture return in place, this would set the stage for flash flooding across southern Utah and scattered instances of severe thunderstorms producing severe wind gusts across northern Utah.
episodes.218533: A complex of strong to locally severe thunderstorms moved across western and into central Kansas on the morning of 8/25 resulting in a lone severe wind report.
